items.title: US military denies Iran hit ship in Strait of Hormuz
items.description: The US military has denied that any of its Navy ships have been hit in the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian state media reported that a US frigate was targeted by two missiles.

items.title: Holocaust survivor says Jews 'have become targets' in Australia
items.description: The Jewish community's experiences of antisemitism have been put on display on the first day of the royal commission triggered by the Bondi Beach terror attack last year.

items.title: Electric vehicle tax discount to be wound back from next year
items.description: A popular tax discount meaning people leasing electric vehicles did not have to pay Fringe Benefits Tax will be wound back — although in the long term, more EV owners will be able to pay a reduced tax rate.

items.title: The treasurer's reality check on Anthony Albanese's bold childcare plan
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has previously committed to delivering universal child care, but Treasurer Jim Chalmers has highlighted concerns about the cost.

items.title: Calls for 'compassion' after newborn twin dies at homeless camp
items.description: A women's health advocate says the death of a baby during childbirth at a homeless camp on the Murrumbidgee River is a "terrible day" for the Wagga Wagga community.

items.title: Officers outraged after investigation uncovers taser security flaw
items.description: Police associations and unions demand urgent action over revelations that a security flaw allows officers to be tracked by criminals with a phone or laptop.

items.title: Sydney Lord Mayor Clover Moore cancels 'globalise the intifada' forum
items.description: The event's cancellation is welcomed by groups representing the Jewish community in New South Wales.

items.title: 'He's a big boy': Socceroos boss defends anti-Trump comments from midfielder
items.description: Australia coach Tony Popovic says it would be "wonderful" if Donald Trump was in the stadium in Seattle when the Socceroos played the United States on June 19, saying the US president's presence would motivate his team.

items.title: Australian businesses falling victim to new type of fraud
items.description: Higher inflation, a war in the Middle East, and a ban on surcharges are crippling small businesses. Now they are falling victim to a modern crime.

items.title: Cruise ship banned from port after three die in suspected virus outbreak
items.description: Three people have died and three people are ill after a suspected outbreak of the rodent-borne virus in the Atlantic Ocean.

items.title: Australia and Japan sign agreements on energy, defence and critical minerals
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Japanese counterpart Takaichi Sanae agreed to bolster cooperation on energy, defence and critical minerals, while warning against economic coercion.

items.title: Sports broadcaster Dennis Cometti farewelled at state memorial service
items.description: A host of high-profile Australians gather at Perth Stadium to pay tribute to one of the nation's most well-known sports broadcasters, Dennis Cometti.

items.title: Sydney man accused of murdering parents and brother denied bail
items.description: Jacky Amazing Feng, 32, faced court for the first time on Monday, following the alleged murder of three family members and attempted murder of another.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby remembered across NT after 'unthinkable trauma'
items.description: The Northern Territory is continuing to grieve the short life of a five-year-old girl today with crowds in Alice Springs to pay tribute by donning pink, her favourite colour.

items.title: Rice is cheap, easy to cook and the main ingredient in these four meals
items.description: Rice doesn't need to play second fiddle. The cheap and simple pantry staple can hold up a whole meal.

items.title: AFL umpire Nick Foot's betting agency role over after tribunal case
items.description: Betting agency Sportsbet announces it will no longer feature current sports administrators or officials in their programming "following feedback".

items.title: Russian woman's husband beat her but police were no help, so she wrote to Putin
items.description: Domestic violence and abuse have been described as an "epidemic" in multiple countries, but analysts argue there is something that sets Russia apart: the government is making things worse.

items.title: ABC staff accept enterprise agreement after pay dispute strike
items.description: ABC staff have struck an enterprise agreement with the broadcaster, bringing an end to a pay dispute that culminated in a 24-hour strike.

items.title: Tim Roth battles Radha Mitchell in gripping Australian action flick
items.description: Shooting in snake-and-spider-infested grass on a Queensland farm, Seven Snipers spooked its stars.

items.title: Quiz: Can you name the typo on the $50 note?
items.description: Take a trip back in time with this week's history quiz.

items.title: Brisbane Lions player under investigation for alleged homophobic slur in VFL
items.description: The AFL faces another homophobic slur case, with a Brisbane Lions player alleged to have used a slur in a VFL game against Coburg.

items.title: Forget the lawn, these mower racers are cutting loose on the race track
items.description: The 2026 All Australian Mower Racing Championships ran for three days over the weekend featuring competitors ready to tear around a track on refurbished ride-ons.

items.title: Netball's 'wishy washy' approach to Pride dulls the message
items.description: Several Super Netball clubs will host their own Pride matches this season, but without an official round to anchor them all a former player and member of the LGBTIQA+ community argues the message may be lost.

items.title: Alleged Anzac Day hecklers face court over 2025 booing
items.description: Witnesses have told a court they were "disgusted" when a group of men interrupted last year's Anzac Day Dawn Service in Melbourne.

items.title: It was a record race time. Moments later spectators were suspicious
items.description: Tasmania's top horse race was run 37 metres shorter than advertised. Officials knew the track distance was likely incorrect but proceeded anyway. This is what happened.
